CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone pain, hypertension and diabetes follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports recurrent kidney stones, this being approximately her 7th or 8th stone. She presented to the emergency room last week with pain that has been up and down. The stone appears to have passed approximately 3 days ago. She denies current blood in urine and denies current pain. She received Percocet at the hospital. She last saw a urologist about a year ago. Regarding hypertension, today's blood pressure was 150/90. Patient reports taking Norvasc 2.5mg regularly and that home blood pressure readings taken 2-3 times per week are usually 130-140/60-70. Doctor discussed possible white coat syndrome. Patient has been having difficulty with diet, consuming fast food and sweets, which she attributes to her busy on-the-go lifestyle and limited time for meal preparation. Regarding diabetes, patient is on Metformin 500mg daily and reports taking it regularly. She does not check blood sugars very often but thinks they have been good. Last A1C was 6.7. Patient also reports history of insomnia, sometimes staying awake worrying about things. She has tried meditation apps which help. She has tried melatonin a couple of times but it did not seem to help much. She does not want to take sleeping pills.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension, Type 2 diabetes, recurrent kidney stones, Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, insomnia.

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5mg daily, Metformin 500mg daily, Percocet (given at hospital), Melatonin (tried previously).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a busy schedule on the go. Consumes fast food and sweets. Sleeps with television on and keeps phone by bed. Uses meditation apps.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure 150/90. Lungs clear bilaterally without crackles. Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur noted, unchanged from prior. Abdomen: no tenderness to palpation. Costovertebral angles: no tenderness on right side.

RESULTS
Last A1C: 6.7. Home blood pressure readings per patient: 130-140/60-70.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stones: Stone appears to have passed. Will obtain urinalysis and urine culture to ensure clearance. Referral to urology with Dr. Harris to evaluate for underlying cause of recurrent stones. Hypertension: Doing well on Norvasc 2.5mg daily, no medication changes needed. Patient has refills through pharmacy. Referral to nutrition consultation to help with dietary management and sodium restriction (goal <2300mg daily). Diabetes: Continue Metformin 500mg daily. Patient instructed to check blood sugars before every meal to help gauge food intake. Insomnia: Start Melatonin 10mg as needed. Reinforce sleep hygiene practices including turning off electronics and maintaining dark, cool room. Follow-up in 3 months.
